claims.title: Coordinate observation is the Walsh projection onto characters supported inside the observed set
claims.scope: uniform Boolean cube with g=(-1)^f and exact coordinate observations
assumptions: Walsh characters use the uniform cube inner product
the observed sigma-field is generated by coordinates in S
nonclaims: the coefficient geometry changes under a nonuniform prior

claims.title: Captured Walsh spectral mass equals the second moment of posterior Boolean bias
assumptions: Parseval and orthogonality are taken under the uniform cube measure
nonclaims: spectral mass alone does not generally determine exact Bayes gap

claims.title: Bayesian posterior absolute bias obeys an exact rational L1-L2 spectral sandwich
claims.scope: uniform Boolean prior with Bayesian K3 gap V(S), absolute bias B=1-2V, and captured spectral mass W
nonclaims: the rational certificate does not require numerical square roots

claims.title: Uniform Boolean influence equals Walsh spectral mass on sets containing the coordinate
claims.scope: finite Boolean sign functions under the uniform cube measure
assumptions: influence is defined by uniform coordinate flips

claims.title: Leave-one-out Bayesian experiment value saturates the upper spectral bound
claims.scope: uniform Boolean cube after observing every coordinate except i
assumptions: the residual posterior cell is a two-point cube edge
nonclaims: generic larger hidden subsets need not saturate the bound

claims.title: Parity captures zero spectral mass and retains Bayes gap one half until full support is observed
claims.scope: three-bit parity under the uniform prior
assumptions: the parity Walsh spectrum is supported only on the full coordinate set
nonclaims: the exact value depends on the symmetric prior

claims.title: Bounded exact Fourier experiment audit
claims.scope: parity, AND, majority, Parseval, influence, leave-one-out saturation, and rational sandwich checks
assumptions: all Walsh coefficients and probabilities use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not a scalability theorem
CI success is not evidence for simulation
